segments.t: In her office at ASK, Andrea welcomes high-fashion model Aymeline Val. While Aymeline insists she is not an ordinary runway model, Andrea seeks to convince her that she has a genuine future as a screen actress. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Merci d'être venue pendant la Fashion Week.
Je ne fais pas de défilés.
Je pensais que tu étais mannequin.
Je suis juste payée pour porter des vêtements.
Mais tu poses dans des magazines.
Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.
D'abord, on ouvre la fenêtre pour fumer.
Ensuite, parlons de ta future carrière.
J'ai déjà un agent pour la publicité.
Ici, il s'agit de vrais artistes.
Tu es une vraie actrice, pas un cintre.
Tu as des nouvelles de Norman?
Deux mois d'attente, c'est une catastrophe.
Let's examine Andrea and Aymeline's conversation step by step.
Merci d'être venue pendant la Fashion Week.
'Thank you for coming during Fashion Week.' In French, thanking someone for a completed visit uses 'thanks of having come', adding a silent '-e' on 'come' for Aymeline.
Je ne fais pas de défilés.
'I do not do fashion shows.' Literally 'parades' or 'processions', the final word is how French refers to runway shows, preceded by 'of' in the negative.
Je pensais que tu étais mannequin.
'I thought you were a model.' Unlike English, French drops 'a' before professions after 'were', and its term meaning 'fashion model' gave English 'mannequin'.
Je suis juste payée pour porter des vêtements.
'I am just paid to wear clothes.' After 'in order to', French uses 'carry' to mean 'wear' clothing—the exact same action covers carrying a bag or wearing a coat.
Mais tu poses dans des magazines.
'But you pose in magazines.' Where English leaves 'magazines' bare, French requires an unspecified 'some' marker in front, paired with two transparent cognates.
Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.
'I work with photographic artists.' Placing 'photographers' right after 'artists' lets one role describe the other in French, where English switches to 'photographic'.
D'abord, on ouvre la fenêtre pour fumer.
'First, we open the window to smoke.' Kicked off by a handy chunk meaning 'at first', the sentence uses 'for' plus 'to smoke' to express purpose in French.
Ensuite, parlons de ta future carrière.
'Next, let's talk about your future career.' Pairing naturally with 'first' from the previous line, the opener means 'next', and the '-ons' ending builds 'let us talk' in one word.
J'ai déjà un agent pour la publicité.
'I already have an agent for advertising.' Notice 'already' sits right after 'have' rather than before it, and the closing term meaning 'advertising' is often clipped in casual speech.
Ici, il s'agit de vrais artistes.
'Here, it is about real artists.' Built from 'it acts itself of', this high-frequency French idiom means 'it is a matter of' or 'this is about'.
Tu es une vraie actrice, pas un cintre.
'You are a real actress, not a coat hanger.' Sitting in front of 'actress', the term meaning 'true' shifts to mean 'genuine' in French, contrasted with a sharp metaphor for 'coat hanger'.
Tu as des nouvelles de Norman?
'Do you have any news about Norman?' Unlike English, where 'news' is uncountable, French treats 'news' as countable items—literally 'some news items of Norman'.
Deux mois d'attente, c'est une catastrophe.

'Two months of waiting, it is a disaster.' Spoken French loves naming a topic like 'two months of waiting' up front and commenting on it with 'it is a catastrophe'. Now let's listen to the whole scene once more from start to finish.
Merci d'être venue pendant la Fashion Week.
Je ne fais pas de défilés.
Je pensais que tu étais mannequin.
Je suis juste payée pour porter des vêtements.
Mais tu poses dans des magazines.
Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.
D'abord, on ouvre la fenêtre pour fumer.
Ensuite, parlons de ta future carrière.
J'ai déjà un agent pour la publicité.
Ici, il s'agit de vrais artistes.
Tu es une vraie actrice, pas un cintre.
Tu as des nouvelles de Norman?
Deux mois d'attente, c'est une catastrophe.
Andrea successfully flatters Aymeline Val into considering cinema representation with ASK, even as production delays complicate the project. See you next time!
À bientôt!
